newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder to buy four ABC newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder to buy four ABC newspapers.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc. said Friday it agreed to buy the Kansas City Star and three other daily newspapers owned by ABC Inc., a division of Walt Disney Co., for $1.65 billion.
It also said it was going to divest Knight-Ridder Information Inc., its on-line information service for business and professional users, which includes Dialogue and DataStar.

The company, whose flagship papers are the Miami Herald and the Philadelphia Inquirer, said the purchase of the newspapers and sale of the on-line service will help it focus on its core newspaper business.

The ABC newspapers include The Kansas City Star, the Fort Worth and Arlington (Texas) Star-Telegrams, the Belleville (Ill.) News-Democrat and The Times Leader in Wilkes-Barre, Pa., it said. Revenue for the group was $500 million in 1996.
Last year, Knight-Ridder sold its Knight-Ridder Financial business news unit for about $275 million to Global Information Corp.
It also got out of the cable television business, reporting an after tax gain earlier in 1997 of $130 million to $150 million.
"The company anticipates completing the sale during 1997," it said. "The transactions will enable Knight-Ridder to focus on its core newspaper business, which is the foundation of the company."

"Kansas City and Fort Worth are models of locally edited, reader-friendly and marketing savvy publications. Both evidence strong online literacy as well. All of these are critical qualities in today's competitive environment," said Chairman Tony Ridder.

He said much of the company's revenus comes from medium and smaller-market newspapers, and the Belleville and Wilkes-Barre papers "will be strong contributors to that group. Both papers have shown steady revenue increases since 1993, with profit growth and strong margins."
ABC was purchased by Disney in 1996 for $19 billion, after which the company has said it planned to divest some of its publishing entities, but has not been specific.

Because of the proposed purchases, Knight-Ridder's earnings during the first 12 months will be diluted by about 10 percent. Minimal dilution will occur during the second year and earnings will show gains during the third year, Knight-Ridder said.
Knight-Ridder said it would finance the deal by issuing $660 million in convertible preferred stock and assuming $990 million of pre-existing debt.
It also said it planned to buy back at least 15 million common shares during the next 12 months.
Knight-Ridder is an international communications company engaged in newspaper publishing, business news and information services, among other things.
Knight-Ridder said the the deal should close within 60 days.
